title: Study of the ameliorative effect of beta-Bisabolene on ischemic stroke via COX-2 with the Keap1/Nrf2 and MAPK pathways.
authors: Zhang, Xingfang; Gao, Liang; Wang, Jianv; Zhang, Wei; Xu, Dong; Wang, Yanhua; Liu, Tianlong; Gao, Kai; Ren, Zhen; Ding, Yi
one_liner_zh: 该文研究beta-Bisabolene对缺血性卒中的抗炎抗氧化作用机制，涉及COX-2、Keap1/Nrf2和MAPK通路，但核心是药物-蛋白相互作用，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且方法以网络药理学和湿实验为主，与本课题无关。
abstract: beta-Bisabolene, a bioactive sesquiterpene extracted from myrrh-a substance utilized for ischemic stroke treatment-has known therapeutic potential. Nevertheless, the exact mechanisms underlying its beneficial effects on ischemic stroke, along with its potential targets, remain to be fully elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic potential of beta-Bisabolene in ameliorating ischemic stroke, identify its potential targets and interactions, and explore the underlying pathways involved. Bioinformatics analyses, including network pharmacology and analysis of GEO transcriptomic datasets, were performed to predict the potential targets and mechanisms of beta-Bisabolene in ischemic stroke treatment. Preliminary computational validation was achieved through molecular similarity comparisons, molecular docking studies, and molecular dynamics simulations. In vitro experiments were then conducted to confirm the protective effects of beta-Bisabolene on microglia injured by oxygen‒glucose deprivation and to validate the findings from the bioinformatics analyses. The results revealed that beta-Bisabolene reduces the levels of the proinflammatory cytokines TNF-alpha, IL-1beta and NO; decreases reactive oxygen species levels; and decreases the expression of COX-2, P38, ERK and Keap1. Moreover, it increases the expression of Arg-1, Nrf2, NQO1 and HO-1. These effects are associated with improved survival rates of oxygen-glucose deprivation-damaged microglia. In conclusion, beta-Bisabolene may exert anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects to ameliorate microglial injury induced by ischemic stroke by antagonizing COX-2 and mediating the MAPK signaling pathway and Keap1/Nrf2 pathway. This study provides valuable insights into the therapeutic potential of beta-Bisabolene for the treatment of ischemic stroke.
abstract_zh: β-红没药烯（beta-Bisabolene）是一种从没药中提取的生物活性倍半萜烯，没药被用于缺血性卒中的治疗，且β-红没药烯具有已知的治疗潜力。然而，其对缺血性卒中产生有益效应的确切机制及其潜在靶点仍有待全面阐明。本研究旨在探讨β-红没药烯在改善缺血性卒中方面的治疗潜力，识别其潜在靶点和相互作用，并探索所涉及的潜在通路。通过生物信息学分析，包括网络药理学和GEO转录组数据集分析，预测了β-红没药烯在缺血性卒中治疗中的潜在靶点和机制。初步计算验证通过分子相似性比较、分子对接研究和分子动力学模拟完成。随后进行了体外实验，以确认β-红没药烯对氧-葡萄糖剥夺损伤的小胶质细胞的保护作用，并验证生物信息学分析的发现。结果表明，β-红没药烯降低了促炎细胞因子TNF-α、IL-1β和NO的水平；降低了活性氧水平；并降低了COX-2、P38、ERK和Keap1的表达。此外，它增加了Arg-1、Nrf2、NQO1和HO-1的表达。这些效应与氧-葡萄糖剥夺损伤的小胶质细胞存活率的提高相关。总之，β-红没药烯可能通过拮抗COX-2并介导MAPK信号通路和Keap1/Nrf2通路，发挥抗炎和抗氧化作用，从而改善缺血性卒中诱导的小胶质细胞损伤。本研究为β-红没药烯治疗缺血性卒中的治疗潜力提供了有价值的见解。
